title: Beyond Accuracy and Complexity: The Effective Information Criterion for Structurally Stable Symbolic Regression
claim: Formulas with equal length and accuracy can differ sharply in structural rationality, so complexity and accuracy alone cannot distinguish them.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: tree, shared scatter plot, tree; red vs blue color coding
description: The figure has three panels in a row. The left panel is a red expression tree for a pathological formula f1. It is deep and has nested sin, cot and abs operators, and a red double-headed arrow marks Tree Depth = 8. A red arrow below it marks Formula Length = 20, and the closed form of f1 is printed under it. The right panel is a blue expression tree for a well-structured formula f2. It has a comparable depth label and the same Formula Length = 20, and its closed form is printed beneath. The center panel is a scatter plot of Prediction against Ground Truth. Red and blue points overlap along the diagonal, and the legend gives test-set R² of 0.984 for f1 and 0.980 for f2. Red and blue separate the two formulas, and the shared plot makes them look equivalent in accuracy.
caption: Formulas with identical complexity and accuracy can exhibit distinct structural rationality. Despite having the same length and $R^2$, the left formula contains pathological nesting, while the right one remains structurally sound, demonstrating that complexity fails to capture structural rationality.
abstract: Symbolic regression (SR) traditionally balances accuracy and complexity, implicitly assuming that simpler formulas are structurally more rational. We argue that this assumption is insufficient: existing algorithms often exploit this metric to discover accurate and compact but structurally irrational formulas that are numerically ill-conditioned and physically inexplicable. Inspired by the structural stability of real physical laws, we propose the Effective Information Criterion (EIC) to quantify formula rationality. EIC models formulas as information channels and measures the amplification of inherent rounding noise during recursive calculation, effectively distinguishing physically plausible structures from pathological ones without relying on ground truth. Our analysis reveals a stark structural stability gap between human-derived equations and SR-discovered results. By integrating EIC into SR workflows, we provide explicit structural guidance: for heuristic search, EIC steers algorithms toward stable regions to yield superior Pareto frontiers; for generative models, EIC-based filtering improves pre-training sample efficiency by 2-4 times and boosts generalization R2 by 22.4%. Finally, an extensive study with 108 human experts shows that EIC aligns with human preferences in 70% of cases, validating structural stability as a critical prerequisite for human-perceived interpretability.
